quizzes.title: Basic Concepts: Charge, Current, Resistance & Ohm's Law

questions.q: SI unit of electrical resistivity (rho) is:
questions.fact: Resistivity rho = R * A / l, so its SI unit is Ohm-meter (Omega*m).
questions.trick: Rho has 'meter' in length/area ratio -> Ohm-meter.
questions.source: RRB JE Electrical Syllabus - Basic Concepts

questions.q: If a wire of resistance R is stretched to double its length (volume constant), new resistance becomes:
questions.fact: With constant volume, R is proportional to l^2; doubling length makes resistance 4R.
questions.trick: Stretch n times -> n^2 times resistance (2^2 = 4).
questions.source: RRB JE Electrical Syllabus - Resistance & Geometry

questions.q: Temperature coefficient of resistance of pure metals is generally:
questions.fact: In pure metals, higher temperature increases lattice vibrations and collisions, increasing resistance.
questions.trick: Metals go UP with heat -> Positive alpha.
questions.source: RRB JE Electrical Syllabus - Temperature Coefficient

quizzes.title: Circuit Laws: KCL, KVL & Series-Parallel Basics

questions.q: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) is a direct consequence of conservation of:
questions.fact: Charge cannot accumulate at a lumped node, so algebraic sum of currents at a node is zero.
questions.trick: KCL = Current = Flow of Charge -> Conservation of Charge.
questions.source: RRB JE Electrical Syllabus - Kirchhoff's Laws

questions.q: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) is based on conservation of:
questions.fact: Sum of potential differences around any closed loop is zero, reflecting energy conservation.
questions.trick: KVL = Voltage (work/energy per unit charge) -> Conservation of Energy.
questions.source: RRB JE Electrical Syllabus - Kirchhoff's Laws
